title: Continuous-variable model for arbitrary image propagation via Dirac-comb expansion in Four-Wave Mixing
authors: Fabián Ramírez-Pacheco, Andrea Basilio-Zárate, Hans Marin Florez, Pablo Solano, Carla Hermann-Avigliano
abstract: We develop a macroscopic continuous-variable model of stimulated four-wave mixing (4WM) yielding closed-form expressions for the mean intensity, variance, and covariance of bright probe and conjugate beams, valid for arbitrary transverse profiles of the pump and seed to all orders in the nonlinear interaction strength. The model uses a Dirac-comb expansion of the pump field, making the photon statistics computable pixel-by-pixel from one set of expressions. In the plane-wave limit, we recover the phase-insensitive amplifier results. Beyond this limit, the formalism explicitly demonstrates the spatial routing of information observed in earlier experiments: the seed angular spectrum is transferred to the twin-beam intensities, whereas the angular spectrum of the squared pump field is transferred to the spatial cross-correlation between the probe and conjugate. We characterize the parameter window of high-fidelity image transfer in the covariance, which is controlled by the seed-to-pump waist ratio and the interaction strength. Our model provides, in one analytical framework, a theoretical account of experiments encoding information in the bright intensities or non-locally in the spatial cross-correlations.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive continuous-variable model for Four-Wave Mixing that calculates quantum correlations (variance and covariance) across arbitrary transverse beam profiles using a Dirac-comb expansion. The theory successfully unifies descriptions of image transfer, showing how information can be encoded in either the measured intensities or non-locally in the spatial cross-correlations. It is significant for its all-order treatment of structured light fields in nonlinear quantum optics.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified theoretical model for characterizing the transverse spatial statistics of quantum-correlated bright twin beams generated via Four-Wave Mixing (4WM). It aims to provide closed-form expressions for mean intensity, variance, and covariance valid for arbitrary pump/seed profiles.
main_result: The formalism successfully extends known results from plane-wave approximations to include complex spatial structuring, demonstrating how information can be encoded in either the bright intensities or non-locally in the spatial cross-correlations via the covariance measurement.
method: The core method involves using a Dirac-comb expansion of the pump field within a continuous-variable framework. This allows for calculating quantum correlation functions (variance and covariance) to all orders in the nonlinear interaction strength.
model_or_system: The physical system is stimulated Four-Wave Mixing (4WM) occurring in an alkali-atom vapor ($\chi^{(3)}$ nonlinearity). The model uses bosonic operators and treats the pump field via a Dirac-comb expansion, enabling pixel-by-pixel computation of quantum statistics.
key_observables: Mean intensity, variance ($\langle\Delta^2 \hat{N}angle$), cross-covariance ($	ext{Cov}(\dots)$), and Intensity-Difference Squeezing (IDS).
important_parameters: Seed-to-pump waist ratio ($\delta$) and interaction strength ($s$). The regime of high fidelity is characterized by $\delta \ll 1$ and $s \lesssim 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations when summing infinite series (e.g., using $\cosh/\sinh$ forms) and assumes the validity of certain limits, such as small coupling parameters or small waist ratios ($\delta \ll 1$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup for image propagation via Fourier imaging detection, the Dirac-comb expansion structure, and plots showing the achievable Image Similarity Score ($S$) versus $(\delta, s)$ space.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the general continuous-variable model using the Dirac-comb expansion to calculate observables like variance and covariance. It validates this by recovering known plane-wave results before demonstrating image transfer capabilities in both intensity (seed imaging) and cross-correlation (covariance imaging).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for quantum optics and open quantum systems because it provides an all-order, spatially resolved theoretical framework to analyze complex nonlinear processes like 4WM. It moves beyond simple plane-wave assumptions to model structured light fields.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Setup for the propagation of arbitrary images in 4WM. An input image is imprinted on the pump and/or seed beams in the object plane defined by the axes (ξx, ξy). A Fourier-imaging lens maps the image to the center of the χ(3) medium, where the 4WM interaction takes place. The second lens propagates the generated probe and conjugate beams to a far-field detection plane defined by the axes (qx, qy), where their intensities and cross-covariances are measured. The boxed insets illustrate energy conservation and the phase-matching condition.
FIG. 2. Illustration of the field’s Dirac-comb expansion at the center of the medium, using the Amazing Quantum logo as an example.

FIG. 3. Intensity and phase profiles of the seed and pump fields in the (ξx, ξy) object plane. The right column shows the intensity and normalized correlations in the (qx, qy) far-field plane. The ℏsymbol is imprinted in the object plane of the seed and mapped to its Fourier components at the center of the medium. The pump profile was Gaussian and spatially larger than the seed at the same plane, with a seed-to-pump width ratio δ = 0.38. The ℏpattern appears in the far-field intensities ⟨ˆ Nq⟩ of both the probe (right) and conjugate (left). FIG. 4. Covariance imaging. In the object plane, the seed is spatially Gaussian, and the pump has the shape required to reproduce the ℏsymbol in the cross-correlation in the low-gain regime, with seed-to-pump width ratio δ = 0.21. The probe and conjugate intensities (right and left Gaussian profiles, respectively) preserve the Gaussian structure of the seed. The normalized correlation, evaluated at qpr = qs and qc = q−qs, reproduces the imprinted ℏpattern. All values of the normalized correlation remain below unity, so the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality is not violated by this configuration; this does not by itself establish classicality, which would require additional witnesses.
FIG. 5. Image similarity S between the computed cross- correlation and the target ℏpattern, as a function of the seed- to-pump width ratio δ and the interaction strength s.
